critique: Story view is black again: the climactic kneeling moment, the keeper's palm and her glowing word are invisible. The overview shows a glowing track cutting between white ash and a huge flat slab of dusty violet glass, with pixel-stepped peach blotches on its far side. The glass is a flat unlit plane with no sky or column reflection. I'm steering toward a guaranteed lit, low, warm-gold-from-below shot of the kneeling figure over a mirror that carries the peach horizon.

suggestions.change: Guarantee a lit frame. Keep exposure 1.3 and skyMode physical, but raise ambient to 0.6 and envLight to 1.0, fogDensity 0.0011, fogColor #7f8fc4. Add a lit fill: a #ffb070 point light, intensity 2.5, range 8 m, at [-1,0.8,-129.5] under the kneeling hand, so the figure is gold-lit from below. Re-aim the story camera to about 1.4 m high, 4 m south of the Wanderer at [-1,1.4,-125.5], looking at [-1,0.4,-130], so the keeper_palm_word is in the lower third and the column is on the horizon.

Fix the pixel-stepped peach blotches. They are z-fighting between glass_sheet (y 0) and decor_glass_patch and decor_column_reflect. Set glass_floor_far y to -0.05, glass_patch to y 0.0, and the column_reflect streak to y 0.02 with polygonOffset. Raise the near colour from #1a2748 to #2a3a66 so it reads as reflected dawn, not violet void. Fade its far end into fog #f0c8b0 so no hard seam shows.

Make the word the hero. Scale palm_word s from 1 to 1.6, keep the white-gold #fff0c8 glyph with its #ffb070 flame at opacity 0.95, and raise its halo to 0.6. Cap the frost coils at opacity 0.6 and 5 m radius so they don't blow out. Add a 0.2 m amber ring pulse around the palm glyph at 1.3 s.

Replace the lone warm_speck with a readable silhouette. Add a #8a6a58 to #d9d4c8 gradient cloak, a #ffb070 rim at 0.4, and a mirrored copy on the glass at 35% opacity. Cut the speck to s 1.2, opacity 0.2 so it doesn't smear the figure.

styleGuide: Palette: void #020308, horizon peach #f0c8b0, horizon blue #8fa8e0, fog #7f8fc4, ash trough #2a3a66, ash crest #b8c8e8, mirror glass #2a3a66 to #f0c8b0, rim glass #bfe8ff, amber #ffb070, white-gold #fff0c8, copper #c4703c. thought: The word in her palm may be what the first lamp was for. I've lost so many names, but maybe this one is the answer to the naming she never finished.
action: Reach through the glass, take the glowing word from her palm, and read it aloud: "Keeper, is this what the lamp was for?"

narration: Your hand sinks through the glass as if through warm water, and your fingers close on the keeper's. The glowing word comes away like a coal, and you read it aloud: "Hearth." Not mouth, not light. The keeper weeps without sound. "Yes. It was never meant to burn. It was meant to be come home to. I could not say it, because I had no one left to come home to." Far south, the whole chain of hollows flares gold, and the amber light answers. Then you reach for the word for the road they lie along, and it is gone, taken at the moment you needed it. North, the light bends toward you and asks, softly: "Who will be its hearth?" The boy steps forward.

facts.description: A palm-sized glowing glyph of an open hand with a flame in its centre, lifted out of the glass. It burns white-gold like a live coal and sits cupped in the Wanderer's hand, throwing warm light up under the hood.
facts.placement: In the Wanderer's right hand, kneeling on glass_floor_far, 3 m north of glass_edge_ring's southern rim.

facts.description: The whole line of glazed hollows far down the track now burns warm gold instead of hard blue. Each beam rises straight up and bends toward the amber light, which swells into a steady hearth-glow on the southern horizon.
facts.placement: On runner_track, between 300 m and 3 km south of the Wanderer, trailing toward south_amber_light.

facts.description: The tall gold-white column has bent its tip slightly toward the Wanderer, like a flame leaning to a draught. Its foot ripples on the glass in slow concentric rings that reach the figures' knees.
facts.placement: About 1.5 km due north of the Wanderer, at the far side of glass_floor_far.

facts.description: The old keeper's upside-down face is wet with tears of gold light, her amber eyes open and her hand now empty and open beneath the Wanderer's. Her braid drifts as if underwater, and she smiles faintly.
facts.placement: Beneath the Wanderer's boots, in glass_floor_far, 3 m north of glass_edge_ring's southern rim.

facts.description: The clear glass boy, 1.3 m tall, has stepped two paces north across the glass toward the light. The white-gold seed in his chest burns bright, and his long shadow reaches back to touch the kneeling Wanderer.
facts.placement: On glass_floor_far, 2 m north of the kneeling Wanderer, facing north_light.

notes: I lifted the glowing hearth glyph out of the glass into the kneeling Wanderer's palm. The glass boy now stands two paces ahead facing the leaning light, with gold warmth washing the south horizon.

The overview shows a snow-white ash slab, a dark violet band of glass with a hard straight edge, and a pale slanted rectangle above the horizon that reads as a glitch. suggestions.change: Guarantee a lit frame. Keep skyMode physical, set ambient 0.75, envLight 1.1, exposure 1.35, and fogColor #8fa0d0 at density 0.0010. Do not add anything black or unfogged near the camera. Story camera: 1.2 m high, 4.5 m south of the Wanderer at [-1,1.2,-125], looking at [-1,0.9,-132]. Give glass_floor_far vertex alpha fading to 0 over the last 150 m at the ash-facing edge. Give its far end the exact fogColor-matched #f0c8b0 peach so it merges into the horizon. Keep the sheets at distinct heights (-0.05, 0, +0.02) with polygonOffset. Make the column streak 6 m wide at opacity 0.45 and fade it out toward the camera so it never blows out the figures.

The boy is 2 m north, backlit by the column: give him a #bfe8ff rim at 0.35 and keep the seed glow at 0.4 so he reads as a clear-glass silhouette. Add his long shadow, #1a2448 at 0.35, stretched south to the Wanderer's knee.

thought: The picture is nearly black; the world has gone dim, but the light asks who will be its hearth. I've lost many names, yet I know what I stand for. The boy is stepping forward and I should ask him the hard thing.
action: Catch the boy's shoulder: "Wait. If you become its hearth, can you ever leave the wick again? Or should we all be the hearth, together?"

narration: You catch the boy's glass shoulder, and it is warm as a stone left in the sun. "Wait," you say, and the word frays in your mouth. You reach for the next one and it is gone: "together", which you had just spoken. The loss hurts, and you stand there with an empty hand. The boy turns and looks at your hand, not at you. "One hearth alone is a mouth," he says. "The keeper proved it. A hearth is a place many come home to. But the wick still needs one hand that can let go, or it will never learn to be lit." The child steps up and sets her cracked lamp beside your coal. Oru Vael, shaking, lays her broad palm over both. North, the tall light lowers its tip, listening.

facts.description: The Wanderer, Oru Vael, the shell child and the clear glass boy kneel or stand in a tight ring around the glowing hearth glyph. Four hands, one broad five-fingered, one broad and lined, one small four-fingered and one glass, rest over the coal, and the light from it throws their shadows outward like spokes across the dark glass.
facts.placement: On glass_floor_far, 3 m north of glass_edge_ring's southern rim, centred on the Wanderer's right hand.

facts.description: The shell child's cracked lamp, burning blue with a gold hairline, is set on the glass beside the hearth coal. Its light and the coal's blend into a steady white-gold pool about 2 m across.
facts.placement: On glass_floor_far, beside hearth_word_coal, at the child's knee.

facts.description: The tall gold-white column has lowered its tip further toward the circle and its glow has softened from hard white to warm gold, like a flame turned down to a hearth fire. Its foot still ripples on the glass in slow rings, now reaching the circle's edge.
facts.placement: About 1.5 km due north of the Wanderer, at the far side of glass_floor_far.

facts.description: The clear glass boy's thin hand rests on the coal beside the Wanderer's. The white-gold seed in his chest pulses in time with it, and a faint thread of light joins chest to coal.
facts.placement: On hearth_word_coal, within hearth_circle, at the Wanderer's right side.

notes: I built the ring of four hands around the glowing coal, with long shadow spokes fanning out over the glass. The cracked lamp sits beside it, and a fine thread links the glass boy's chest to the coal.

critique: The story view is a flat near-black void again, so the hearth circle (the coal, the four hands, the boy's hand) is invisible. The overview shows a pale ash slab, a violet-blue slab, and a thin dark trench with two blown white-gold blobs. The whole scene looks washed out and flat. I'm pushing for a guaranteed lit, low shot of the glowing coal ringed by four hands on a mirror that carries the peach horizon, with the blobs tamed into soft pools.

suggestions.change: Guarantee a lit frame. Keep skyMode physical, skyBottom #f0c8b0, skyTop #1a2a5a, ambient 0.8, envLight 1.1, exposure 1.3, bloom 0.13, fogColor #8fa0d0 at density 0.0010. Story camera: 1.1 m high, 4 m south of the coal at [-0.8,1.1,-126], looking at [-0.8,0.4,-131] so the coal, the four hands and the column on the horizon are all in frame. Nothing black or unfogged near the lens. If the frame is below 8% luminance, raise ambient to 1.0.

Tame the blown white blobs. Cut the central glow from 2.2 m at 0.55 to 1.6 m at 0.35 and the outer pool from 5 m at 0.18 to 4 m at 0.12. Keep the four hands readable, with a #ffb070 rim at 0.3 on the skin tones. Make the shadow spokes #1a2448 at 0.3, running south and fading out by 6 m, so the ring reads as a gathering and not a lens flare.

Make the mirror read as glass. Put a #f0c8b0 horizon band at the far end, with a smoothstep to #2a3a66 near the camera. Add a soft ash-to-glass seam at z -132, where decor_seam_mist is at 0.18 opacity. Add a 6 m wide #fff0c8 column streak at 0.4 opacity that fades out within 8 m of the camera. Also tone down the hard top edge of the violet slab in the overview by extending the fade to 300 m.
Stop the snow-white overview slab. Cap the crest at #9fb0d6, multiply by 0.7 beyond 100 m, and fade the tile edges to #5a70aa over 60 m, so the plain sinks into the far ground in the overview.

Mood: cold silent dawn, one white-gold column answering across a mirror floor, a small warm hearth of hands in the foreground. Light: low raking north sun, backlit figures with warm rims, gold uplight from coal and glyphs, long soft shadow spokes, bloom 0.13, no blown blobs, never a black frame. Materials: mirror glass carrying peach sky, matte ash, copper, hair-thin threads. Soft edges, no hard rectangles. Motifs: vastness, reflection, embers, breath from the dark.
unlockReason: Already at the top tier; the limits aren't what holds the picture back.

notes: I've lit the frame with the brighter dawn settings. I also softened the hearth's glow pools and shadow spokes, and I smoothed the mirror's near-to-horizon gradient and the ash tile edges. I couldn't change the camera, because polish passes can't move the Wanderer.

thought: The picture is nearly black, so the world is barely formed. I've lost many names, but the coal in my hand is still here, and the wick needs one hand that can let go. I'll offer to be that hand.
action: I say: "I'll be the hand that lets go. Light the wick from my coal, and when it's lit, all of you call me home."

narration: You lift the coal in your palm and say it: "I'll be the hand that lets go. Light the wick from my coal, and when it's lit, all of you call me home." The coal flares, and the wick of light from the boy's chest runs through your fingers into it. You reach for the word for what you are doing, the lighting, and it is gone. That one hurts: your hand holds fire and has no name for it. The north light lowers its tip to the glass, and the gold thread climbs it like flame up a candle. Oru Vael says your name for you, a name you never had, and the child answers it. The glass boy looks at your open hand and says quietly, "Now I must pay too."

facts.description: A braided thread of white-gold fire runs from the hearth coal across the glass for 1.5 km to the foot of the north light. The tall column's tip has bent down to meet it, and flame climbs the column from base to tip like a candle taking light.
facts.placement: From hearth_word_coal on glass_floor_far, due north to north_light.

facts.description: The palm-sized glowing glyph of an open hand with a flame at its centre burns fiercely in the Wanderer's open right hand. A braided wick of fire pours from it northward, and the Wanderer's fingers are lit translucent red-gold.
facts.placement: In the Wanderer's right hand, kneeling on glass_floor_far, 3 m north of glass_edge_ring's southern rim.

facts.description: The clear glass boy's fingertips and hem have gone cloudy and are shedding fine glass motes that drift north along the wick. The seed in his chest burns steady.
facts.placement: On boy_lamp_figure at the Wanderer's right side, within hearth_circle.

notes: I lit the wick: a braided white-gold thread now runs from the coal north across the glass to the column, with flame climbing the column's body. The glass boy's edges shed fine motes that drift north along the thread, and I raised the fill light a little so the frame stays lit.

critique: The story view is a pure near-black void again, so the lit wick and the boy's fading glass motes are invisible. The overview shows a snow-white ash slab beside a flat lavender sky-colored plane, with a bright blob at the hearth and a thin gold wick cutting the glass to the horizon. The wick is the right idea, but the scene is still washed out and there's no depth. I'm pushing for a guaranteed lit low shot along the wick toward the burning column, with a soft mirror that fades into the peach horizon.

suggestions.change: Guarantee a lit frame. Keep skyMode physical, skyTop #1a2a5a, skyBottom #f0c8b0, ambient 1.0, envLight 1.2, exposure 1.4, bloom 0.13, fogColor #8fa0d0 at density 0.0009. Aim the story camera 1.1 m high, 4 m south of the coal at [-0.8,1.1,-126], looking at [-0.8,0.8,-135], so the coal, the glass boy's shedding fingertips and the wick running north are in frame. Nothing black or unfogged near the lens. If the frame is below 8% luminance, raise ambient to 1.2.

Remove the flat lavender plane look. Make the mirror carry the sky with a vertical gradient from #2a3a66 near the camera to #f0c8b0 at the horizon. Fade its far 200 m into fog so no hard edge shows. Fade the side edges over 150 m with vertex alpha. Put the glass at y -0.05, decor_glass_ring_disc at 0 and decor_column_reflect at +0.02 with polygonOffset, so nothing z-fights. Make the column reflection 6 m wide at opacity 0.4, fading out within 10 m of the lens.

Make the wick read as a lit thread, not a flat line. Narrow the core to 0.12 m of #fff0c8 and keep the 2.4 m glow at opacity 0.18, with perspective fade past 400 m. Add a faint mirrored wick under the glass at 35% opacity, and a few drifting gold sparks along the first 20 m. Cap the hearth sprite at 1.2 m and opacity 0.3 so the coal stops being a blown white blob.

Make the glass boy's shedding visible. Raise the motes from size 0.05 to 0.09 and the count to 140. Colour them #cfeaff with a few #fff0c8, drifting north along the wick for 15 m, and fade them out. Give the boy's cloudy hem and fingertips a #bfe8ff rim at 0.35 and keep his chest seed at 0.4, so he reads as clear glass dissolving into light.

styleGuide: Palette: void #020308, horizon peach #f0c8b0, horizon blue #8fa8e0, fog #8fa0d0, ash trough #2a3a66, ash crest #8fa0c8, mirror glass #2a3a66 to #f0c8b0, rim glass #bfe8ff, amber #ffb070, white-gold #fff0c8, copper #c4703c. Mood: cold silent dawn, one white-gold column taking light from a thread of fire across a mirror floor, a small warm hearth of hands in the foreground. Light: low raking north sun, backlit figures with warm rims, gold uplight from coal and wick, soft shadow spokes, bloom 0.13, no blown blobs, never a black frame. Materials: mirror glass carrying peach sky, matte ash, copper, hair-thin threads. Soft edges, no hard rectangles. Motifs: vastness, reflection, embers, dissolving glass motes.
unlockReason: Already at the top tier; the limits aren't what is holding the picture back.

notes: I lit the frame (ambient, env light and fog set as asked) and set the glass, ring disc and column reflection at separate heights so they don't fight. The wick is now a thin 0.12 m core with a faint glow, a 35% mirrored copy and drifting gold sparks. The hearth sprite is capped. The boy's motes are bigger, more numerous and fade out over 15 m. I couldn't aim the camera: there is no op for it, and no moving the Wanderer this turn.

assessment: The writing has reached its climax and it's good: turn 35 pays off the name-spending with Oru giving the Wanderer a name "you never had," and the boy's "Now I must pay too" is a real hook. But the audience has watched a black rectangle for six of the last six turns (30, 32–35); the only visible thing is the overview, where the "mirror floor" is a flat lavender slab with a gold line scratched across it. Worse, the core cast isn't in the scene at all: oru_vael, boy_lamp_figure/boy_on_rim and keeper_palm_word are all still NOT YET BUILT, so even a working camera would show the Wanderer alone talking to nobody. The story has outrun the world by about ten turns; the next five turns must be spent making the climax visible before it ends.
narrative: The arc is sound: keep turn 35's two threads as the spine of the ending — the Wanderer is now named only by others, and the boy's debt is unpaid. Retire the "you reach for a word and it is gone" beat; it has run turns 26–35 and the audience has it. Replace it with the inverse: every few turns someone gives the Wanderer a name or word back (the child, the old keeper, Oru), so the ending is earned restoration, not more loss. Decide the boy's price concretely by turn 38 (he dissolves into the wick, or stays as the column's keeper, or becomes a shell child himself), and let Oru make a choice about it rather than weep. Use 40–44 for the column fully lit and the plain transformed (the forty-one hollows become a road of hearths), then 45–50 for the ride south to the amber Hearth with whoever survives, ending on the Wanderer asked "who are you" and answering with the name they were given.
visual: Stop writing critiques that begin "I'm steering toward" and end with a black frame; four turns of identical notes with zero change means the diagnosis is wrong. The black is almost certainly occlusion or fog, not exposure: the camera follows a kneeling Wanderer whose eye line is inside the glass slab or the hood/coal sprite, or fog density at the camera makes #020308 void. Direct the Builder to: make glass_floor_far a single thin plane at y=0 with no thickness or second mirrored copy above it, set fog near distance beyond 20 m, and put the Wanderer standing, not kneeling. Second priority, once lit: the mirror must actually reflect — the overview shows a matte lavender plane with no column, no peach horizon, no second sky; a dark reflective material with the column's reflection as a real mirrored mesh will do more for awe than any palette tweak. Drop the ash slab's pure white; it's blowing out the overview and reads as snow, not ash.
builder: Three fixes in priority order. 1) Build the people: oru_vael (broad, white braid, amber lamp at hip, scorched wristband) and boy_lamp_figure (1.3 m, clear glass, white-gold seed in chest, fading hem motes) have been "NOT YET BUILT" since turns 11 and 21 — the hearth_circle of four hands cannot exist without them. 2) Kill the black frame yourself: render the story view from the follow camera before submitting, check whether the camera is inside glass_floor_far, the ring disc or the mirrored wick copy, and if so thin or remove them; also lower fog density near the camera. 3) Make the climax read at scale: north_light should be a visible column with flame climbing it, the wick should have a glowing core plus a soft ground pool, and the glass should mirror the column and the four figures upside down. Also build keeper_palm_word and the reflection_keeper face under the glass; the overview suggests neither exists.
wanderer: You have been kneeling in roughly the same spot since turn 31, which is likely why the camera sees nothing — stand up and move. Next turn, rise and walk north along the lit wick toward the column, boy beside you, so the follow camera gets a travelling shot with the flame ahead and the hearth circle behind. Stop asking two-part questions; you've answered the big one, so act and let the Narrator react: pick up the child's lamp, take the boy's cloudy hand, say the name Oru gave you aloud. Press on the boy's debt — ask Oru directly what she will give so he doesn't pay alone — and look south at least once so the audience sees the gold chain of hollows and the Hearth you'll ride home to.
experience: The viewer experience right now is a side feed of good prose next to a black screen, which is the single worst failure state this format has. Whoever can set camera or Wanderer position: move the Wanderer to standing at least 2 m from any glass edge or disc, raise the follow camera to 1.6 m eye height with a 0.1 m near plane, and verify a non-black pixel average before the turn is published; if a frame is still black, fall back to the overview camera rather than show void. Once lit, watch bloom at the hearth — the turn-35 overview has one blown white blob at the coal; cap emissive and let the wick line carry the brightness. Pacing is fine in the text, but each of the next five turns needs one new visible thing (Oru, the boy, the mirrored column, the flame climbing, the south chain) so the audience can finally see the cast they've been reading about.

thought: The picture is black because I've been kneeling too long. I need to rise and move, and the boy says he must pay too. I won't let him pay alone.

thought: The boy keeps looking at Oru, not the fire. His hem is still cloudy, so his debt isn't paid. I should find out what he wants from her.
action: Stop walking, kneel by the boy and ask softly: "Why are you looking at your mother, and not the fire? What do you still owe?"

narration: You kneel on the wick and ask softly what he still owes. The boy's eyes stay on Oru. "My glass," he says. "The fire is lit from my seed. When it reaches the column, the glass must stay as its lamp, and I with it. I was looking at her to learn her face once more." He gives you back a word, "lighting", warm in your mouth like a returned coal. Oru Vael kneels, the first time you have seen her choose without weeping. She lays her broad palm over his seed. "No. I will be its keeper. You will be flesh, and grow cold, and come home." The seed's white-gold shivers, and the glass at his wrist turns to pale skin.

facts.description: The glass boy's left wrist and hand have turned from clear glass to warm pale skin with faint pearly veins, five-fingered like a human child's. The change creeps slowly up his forearm in a fine line of white-gold light, while the rest of him stays clear glass.
facts.placement: On the boy beside the kneeling Wanderer, on the wick on glass_floor_far, 60 m north of hearth_circle.

facts.description: Oru Vael kneels on the glowing wick with her broad lined palm pressed flat over the white-gold seed in the boy's chest. Gold light seeps between her fingers and runs up her wrist in fine wick-like coils, and her white braid lifts as in a warm updraft.
facts.placement: On the wick, facing the boy, 1 m east of the kneeling Wanderer.

facts.description: The north column's flame has stooped to about 20 m above the glass, swaying toward the walkers like a hand held out and listening. Gold light floods across the dark floor and throws long shadows behind the group, with warmth felt on the face.
facts.placement: About 1.2 km north of the Wanderer, at the foot of north_light.

notes: Oru kneels with her broad palm over the boy's seed, gold coils climbing her wrist, and the boy's left hand is now warm pale skin with a thin line of light creeping up the forearm. action: Step to the stone hearth ring, kneel, and lay my coal in its centre. What is carved into the stones?

narration: You step over the knee-high blocks and kneel at the glass centre of the ring. The stones are carved with open hands, forty-one of them, one for each hollow on the road, and a forty-second hand is left blank, its fingers unfinished. Beneath it, in the old keeper's clumsy script: "Set the coal. Then say who comes home." You lay the coal down, and the glass drinks it, warm as a hearth stone in winter. Ilen, the name Oru gave you, rises in your throat. The flame overhead stoops until its tip touches the coal. The boy's small hand tightens in yours, and he whispers, "The blank hand is mine."

critique: The frame is finally lit, but it is blown out. The hearth ring is a white cog with no stone detail, the glass floor is flat cream instead of a dark mirror, and the leaning flame is a hard-edged beige slab. A hard violet stripe cuts the horizon where the far ground meets the sky. The goal needs depth: a dark reflective floor, a ring of warm stone lit from one side, and a column that is a soft tapering flame rather than a box.

suggestions.change: Pull the exposure back: exposure 1.0, ambient 0.7, envLight 0.8, sunIntensity 1.1, sunColor #ffc890, sunDirection [0.15,0.12,-0.98], bloom 0.15, fogDensity 0.0004. Set skyTop #1a2a5a and keep skyBottom #f0c8b0, so a visible gradient replaces the flat cream wash and the ring's carved hands and shadows can read.

Rebuild the leaning flame as a soft tapering volume, not a box. Use a cone or cylinder with a radial alpha falloff (centre #fff0c8 at 0.6 opacity, edge 0 opacity) and a base width of about 6 m narrowing to a tip. Add a gentle vertical flicker. Remove any flat rectangular plane. The column should glow hot gold-white at the core and fade into peach at the edges, with no visible hard outline.

Darken the near glass to #2a3a66 and blend it to #f0c8b0 only beyond 400 m, so the ring and figures sit on dark mirror. Recolour decor_far_ground to #c9b4c4, the horizon haze colour, so the violet #8f6fb0 stripe disappears. Raise decor_horizon_band to y 6, h 80, #f0c8b0, opacity 0.5 to blend the ground into the sky.

Stop the ring blowing out. Make the blocks #8a8478 with roughness 0.9 and no emissive, so the sun side shows warm #ffc890 and the shadow side stays cool #5a5a78. Keep the amber trim at emissiveIntensity 0.3. Set the coal sprite to opacity 0.15 and the hearth pool to s 3, so the dark glass centre and the carved hands are visible and the coal reads as the single bright point.

styleGuide: Palette: horizon peach #f0c8b0, dawn blue #8fa8e0, fog #8fa0d0, ash trough #2a3a66, ash crest #8fa0c8 (never white), mirror glass #2a3a66 to #f0c8b0, stone #8a8478, amber #ffb070, white-gold #fff0c8, copper #c4703c. Mood: cold silent dawn, a small hearth of hands walking a white-gold wick across a dark mirror floor to a leaning column of flame. Light: low raking north sun, backlit warm rims, exposure about 1.0, nothing blown to flat white, brightness held by the thin wick and the coal only. Gradient sky, never a black frame or a hard stripe at the horizon. Materials: dark mirror glass, matte ash and stone, copper, hair-thin threads. Motifs: reflection, embers, open hands, glass turning to flesh.
unlockReason: Already at the top tier (5/5). Triangle and byte budgets have room; lights are capped, so this turn's lighting fixes use existing lights and materials.

notes: I pulled the exposure down, then rebuilt the flame as a soft tapering volume with no box. The glass is now dark mirror, the ring is matte stone lit from one side, and the violet stripe is gone.

assessment: Turn 40 lands the story exactly where it should be: coal in the hearth, a forty-second blank hand, and "say who comes home" is a clean final question with ten turns left. But the audience has seen one lit frame since turn 24, and that frame (turn 40) is a blown-out white cog on a cream floor with the Wanderer kneeling alone; the overview is still black. Oru, the boy and the child, the whole emotional cast of the climax, are not in the scene, so the most important image of the piece currently shows a person talking to an empty ring. The prose has also started looping on one refrain ("comes back warm like a coal returned" four turns running). The last ten turns must freeze the lighting rig, put the family in the ring, and spend the words on names that have never been spoken.
narrative: The ending is set up; now pay it with the one thing you've withheld for 40 turns: the boy has no name, and neither does the child. Make "say who comes home" cost Oru, not the Wanderer: she must speak the son's name she has not said in forty-one winters, and give the child a true name instead of "Daughter," and that is what fills the forty-second hand. Resolve the contradiction between turn 31 ("I will stay beside you, nameless") and turn 35 ("I'll be the hand that lets go"): decide whether Ilen stays as the north hearth's keeper while the family rides south to the amber Hearth, or lets the old keeper's reflection take the post and walks home with them; either is good, but pick one by turn 46. Retire the "coal returned" refrain entirely; each remaining turn should introduce a new image (the column settling into a low hearth-fire, the glass floor losing its mirror, the forty-one hollows going dark one by one as lamps are no longer needed). Target: 41–44 naming and lighting, 45–47 the keeper's rest and the cost, 48–50 a quiet coda on the road south at dawn.
visual: Stop changing the rig. You have toggled sky mode, exposure and background every turn since 37 and the result is void, void, void, then blowout; pick one setup (gradient sky, one low directional sun from the north behind the column, exposure 1.0, no fog above 50% density) and do not touch it again unless a rendered frame proves it broken. The biggest available win is contrast: a genuinely dark mirror floor (#2a3a66) under warm stone and four rim-lit figures, with the column as the only bright thing. In the turn-40 frame the floor is cream and the ring is white; if the Builder's "40 polish" truly fixed this, confirm it against an actual frame before writing the next critique, because the overview is still black and something is still occluding or overexposing. Kill the hard horizon stripe by matching far-floor colour to the sky's bottom gradient band.
builder: The scene at the hearth ring has no cast. Build, inside foot_hearth_ring this turn: Oru Vael kneeling (broad, white braid, red-brown wrap as in turns 12–24), the boy at 1.3 m with his left forearm pale skin and the rest clear lit glass, and the shell child standing on the south block with her gold-cracked lamp; place them so none stand between the chase camera and the Wanderer. Clear the NOT YET BUILT backlog that still matters for the finale (oru_vael, boy_wrist_turning_flesh, kneeling_wanderer); drop the shaft-era ones (oru_on_terrace, boy_on_back, keeper_palm_word) as moot. Make hearth_ring_carvings legible: 41 small gold hand decals on the block faces plus one dark unfinished hand on the north block with a faint amber scratch line beneath it, visible at 3 m. The overview camera is returning black: it is likely inside the glass floor or beyond the far clip of a 1.5 km floor; raise it, point it at the ring with the column in frame, and check the frame before submitting.
wanderer: You have "walked north along the wick" in three of the last five turns; the walking is over, so stop moving and start finishing. Ask the questions only the ending can answer: ask Oru to say the boy's name aloud, ask the child what name she would like to be called home by, and ask the reflection keeper whether she can rest now. Push on your own bargain: you promised both to stay beside the light and to be the hand that lets go; ask the light which it needs, and choose. Look back south once near the end and ask what the road is for now that no one needs to carry.
experience: Ten turns of climax have produced one visible frame, and that frame is over-exposed with the cast missing; before anything else, Builder and Designer must produce one confirmed lit frame with four figures in it, then lock the rig for the remaining turns. Frame the finale from a low three-quarter angle south-east of the ring, eye height, Wanderer at frame-left third, Oru and boy centre, column rising out of the top edge, so the kneeling action and the hand carvings are both readable. Trim the Narrator's recurring "comes back like a coal returned" and the Wanderer's "walk north along the wick" so each turn's message tells the audience something new. Keep the overview camera alive: if it is black at turn 50 the audience never sees the whole road from the amber Hearth to the north flame, which is the one wide shot this story has been building toward.

thought: The ring wants a name for who comes home. The blank hand is the boy's, so Oru should speak his name and finish the carving.
action: Turn to Oru: "Say your son's name aloud, Oru Vael, and press his small hand into the blank stone. Who comes home?"

narration: You turn to Oru Vael and ask who comes home. Her mouth works around a silence forty-one winters deep. Then she kneels, takes the boy's small warm hand, and presses it into the blank stone. "Tamsin," she says. The name cracks as it leaves her, and she sags like a cord cut. The stone drinks it, and the unfinished fingers carve themselves, glowing gold. She turns to the child. "And you are Wren, who came when I could not." The child's lamp goes clear and steady. You reach for no word, and none is taken. The flame overhead sighs and begins to settle.

facts.description: The forty-second open-hand glyph on the northernmost block is now fully carved, its fingers finished, and glows warm gold like the other forty-one. A small child's palm is pressed into it, and beneath it a freshly cut name in shallow letters: Tamsin.
facts.placement: On the northernmost block of foot_hearth_ring, replacing the unfinished hand.

facts.description: The boy, now named Tamsin, is a small living child about 1.3 m tall, with warm pale skin, dark tousled hair and a faint glass shimmer fading from his chest where the seed burned. He kneels with his right hand pressed to the stone and his left held by the Wanderer.
facts.placement: Kneeling at the northern block of foot_hearth_ring, beside the Wanderer.

facts.description: The shell child's cracked lamp has turned from blue to clear, steady white-gold, its hairline crack sealed with a thread of gold. She stands beside Oru, her pale shell face lit softly.
facts.placement: At foot_hearth_ring, west side, beside Oru Vael.

facts.description: The north column's flame has begun to settle, shortening and widening from a tall flame into a broad, low, warm hearth-fire about 6 m high, swaying gently over the ring and shedding drifting sparks.
facts.placement: Directly above foot_hearth_ring at the foot of north_light.

notes: The ring now has its cast: Tamsin kneels at the north block with his palm on a finished gold hand and a fresh name beneath, Oru kneels beside, and Wren stands in her steadied white-gold lamplight. The north flame has settled into a broad low hearth-fire.

thought: The family is named and whole, but I promised both to stay and to let go. I must ask the light which it needs and choose.
action: Look up at the settling flame and ask: "You are lit now. Do you need me to stay beside you, or to let go? Tell me, and I'll choose."

narration: You look up and ask. The flame does not answer in borrowed voices this time. It crackles in one low, plain tone, like a fire talking to itself in a kitchen. "Stay, and I will be tended. Let go, and I will learn to tend myself. I would like to learn." The mirror of the glass floor clouds from the edges inward, and your upside-down reflection thins until only the old keeper remains, standing now, not kneeling. She looks up at the fire and says, "I will sit with it. I know how." Far south, one hollow in the long gold chain goes dark, gently, like a lamp put out at bedtime.

thought: The flame wants to learn to tend itself. I promised to be the hand that lets go, so I should choose that, and ask the keeper whether she can rest.
action: I say: "Then I let go, and you learn. Keeper, may you rest now? And Wren, what name would you like to be called home by?"

narration: You say it: let go, and learn. The keeper beneath the glass bows her head. "I have wanted to be told that for a very long time." She lifts her folded hands, and they come apart into gold motes that rise through the clouded floor like sparks up a chimney. Then you turn to the child. Wren thinks, lamp held against her chest. "Wren is the name for coming. I would like one for staying," she says, and looks at Oru. Oru laughs, wet and startled. "Wren Hearthward," she says. The lamp brightens, and the last mirror in the glass goes out.
